persona.bio: Dani, 34, runs a mobile dog grooming van on her own in a suburb of Atlanta. Six or seven dogs a day. Clients book by text, and she answers the same questions all day: prices by breed, how long it takes, whether she does nails only, how to reschedule. She sends reminder texts the night before, writes a short note after each groom about matting or skin, and posts before and after photos on Instagram. Bookings live in a paper diary and her phone's calendar. She has never used AI.

path.role: You run your own mobile dog grooming van, handling bookings, appointment reminders, social media and messages to clients all day from your phone and paper diary.

steps.firstStep: I’m a mobile dog groomer who runs my own grooming van. My clients text me to change or ask about appointments. Write a short, friendly text reply I can send from my phone. Keep it under 40 words and sound warm and professional. Here is the client’s message: [paste the client’s message here]

steps.note: I run my own mobile dog grooming van. I mostly write to my clients, who are dog owners, by text on my phone. I answer booking questions, move appointments, send reminders and post on social media. I like a friendly, warm tone that is short and plain, usually two or three sentences. I sign off simply. Never add details I did not give you, like prices, times, breeds or names. If something is missing, put it in square brackets so I can fill it in. Always give me one version I can read and send myself, and tell me if you need more information first.

steps.title: Your client texts, saved once on your phone
steps.read: Your client replies now live on your phone’s keyboard, each one a few letters away. You stop typing the same answer from scratch many times a day. Every reply is still yours to read and change before it goes out, so it sounds like you and fits the dog and the day.

safeUse: Never type a client’s full name, home address, phone number or door codes into a chat tool. Use [square brackets] and fill them in yourself.
Keep dog health details, like medication or a vet’s diagnosis, out of the chat. Ask for a draft and use your own judgment on the dog’s care.
Never type payment details or bank information into a chat tool.
Read every reply, reminder and post before it goes out, and check the day, time and dog’s name against your diary.
Check any price or timing against your own rates before you send it.

design.today: You answer client messages all day, each one from scratch, from your phone. They include price and timing questions by breed and requests to move a booking.
design.newWay: Your most common replies are saved on your phone, so each one is a few letters away. You pick the right one, fill in the dog's name and the day, read it, and send it yourself. Answers about price and timing by breed stay the same every time, and you stop retyping them.

steps.goal: Pick your ten most common messages, such as moving a booking, price by breed, how long a groom takes and how to book.
Get ChatGPT ready on your phone so you have somewhere to turn those ten into clean replies.
Write your ten replies in your own voice, with gaps for the dog's name, day and price.
Save the ten replies so each one is a few letters away in any text or chat.
Check the prices and timings by breed in each saved reply against your own price list.

design.checkPoint: You read every reply and fill in the gaps before you send it, and nothing is sent by itself.

design.today: You text appointment reminders by hand from your paper diary. You check your day's appointments in the diary and your text messages.
design.newWay: You keep your reminder wording as one saved reply with gaps for name, dog, day and time. Each evening you look at your diary, tap the saved reply, fill in the gaps and send it yourself. The wording stays the same every time, and you only have the details to type.

Turn your usual reminder into a short friendly message with gaps for the details.
Save the reminder so it is a few letters away when you text.
Choose a set time in your day to go through the diary and send the next day's reminders.
